findings.evidence: `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean:23-26` makes the pole-set/enlargement claim; `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean:86-92` defines `HasCauchyPV` as `∃ S : Finset ℂ, ...`, and `rg` finds no enlargement or pole-set witness theorem in the file.
findings.fix: Rewrite this as motivation only: call `S` a finite excision set, and say a prescribed set can be used as a witness once its integrability and tendsto clauses have been proved.
findings.issue: The module doc says a prescribed pole set witnesses the existential directly and describes enlargement as inert, but `HasCauchyPV` only existentially quantifies a `Finset ℂ` satisfying the two clauses and this file has no theorem showing a pole set satisfies them or that enlarging a witness is inert.

findings.evidence: `CauchyPrincipalValueOn.lean:161-167` documents a no-on-curve-singularity condition, while the statement has only `hf_int : IntervalIntegrable ...`.
findings.fix: Remove the singularity claim or qualify it as an external source of the `IntervalIntegrable` hypothesis under additional hypotheses not stated here.
findings.issue: The docstring for `HasCauchyPV.of_integrable` says it applies when no singularity of `f` lies on `γ`, which is what secures integrability, but the theorem assumes only `IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f (γ t) * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b`.

summary: The new declarations are documented, but two comments still overstate analytic content that the file does not state or prove.
